## Declarations and implementations

```plato

    //==
    // # Sphere, shell, cap, and ellipsoid bodies
    //
    // Volume, surface area, bounds, centroid, containment, nearest-point and support
    // bodies for the types declared in `spatial-primitives.types.plato`. The frame and disk-extent
    // helpers, and the conventions governing every body here, are in the shared
    // section above.

    //==
    // # Sphere
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere

    // (4/3) * pi * r^3.
    Volume(s: Sphere): Number
        => 4.0 / 3.0 * Number.Pi * s.Radius.Cube;

    // 4 * pi * r^2.
    SurfaceArea(s: Sphere): Number
        => 4.0 * Number.Pi * s.Radius.Square;


    // The cube of side 2r about the centre.
    Bounds(s: Sphere): Bounds3D
        => CenteredBounds(s.Center, s.Radius, s.Radius, s.Radius);

    // True when the point is within Radius of the centre; boundary inclusive.
    Contains(s: Sphere, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => s.Center.Between(point).MagnitudeSquared <= s.Radius.Square;

    // The query point when it lies in the ball, otherwise its radial projection
    // onto the sphere.
    ClosestPoint(s: Sphere, point: Point3D): Point3D
        => s.Contains(point)
        ? point
        : s.Center + s.Center.Between(point).Normalize * s.Radius;

    // The point of the sphere farthest along `direction`.
    Support(s: Sphere, direction: Direction3D): Point3D
        => s.Center + direction.Vector * s.Radius;

    //==
    // # SphericalShell

    // (4/3) * pi * (R^3 - r^3).
    Volume(s: SphericalShell): Number
        => 4.0 / 3.0 * Number.Pi * (s.OuterRadius.Cube - s.InnerRadius.Cube);

    // BOTH boundary spheres: 4*pi*(R^2 + r^2). The shell is a solid region with two
    // boundary components, and `SurfaceArea` is the area of its whole boundary.
    SurfaceArea(s: SphericalShell): Number
        => 4.0 * Number.Pi * (s.OuterRadius.Square + s.InnerRadius.Square);


    // The bounds of the outer sphere.
    Bounds(s: SphericalShell): Bounds3D
        => CenteredBounds(s.Center, s.OuterRadius, s.OuterRadius, s.OuterRadius);

    // True when the distance from the centre lies in [InnerRadius, OuterRadius];
    // both boundaries inclusive.
    Contains(s: SphericalShell, point: Point3D): Boolean
    {
        var distanceSquared = s.Center.Between(point).MagnitudeSquared;
        return distanceSquared >= s.InnerRadius.Square
            && distanceSquared <= s.OuterRadius.Square;
    }

    //==
    // # SphericalCap
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_cap

    // The cap's height along the axis: R * (1 - cos theta). Runs from 0 (empty) to
    // 2R (the whole ball, at theta = pi).
    CapHeight(c: SphericalCap): Number
        => c.Sphere.Radius * (1.0 - c.PolarAngle.Cos);

    // The radius of the flat cutting disk: R * sin theta.
    CapBaseRadius(c: SphericalCap): Number
        => c.Sphere.Radius * c.PolarAngle.Sin;

    // (pi * h^2 / 3) * (3R - h).
    Volume(c: SphericalCap): Number
        => Number.Pi * c.CapHeight.Square * (3.0 * c.Sphere.Radius - c.CapHeight) / 3.0;

    // The curved cap 2*pi*R*h PLUS the flat cutting disk pi*a^2, because the solid
    // cap's boundary includes the plane that closes it (the declaration says the
    // cap is "closed by the cutting plane").
    SurfaceArea(c: SphericalCap): Number
        => 2.0 * Number.Pi * c.Sphere.Radius * c.CapHeight
        + Number.Pi * c.CapBaseRadius.Square;

    // On the axis, at 3*(2R - h)^2 / (4*(3R - h)) from the SPHERE's centre. Checks
    // out at both ends: h = R gives 3R/8 (the hemisphere) and h = 2R gives 0 (the
    // whole ball). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_cap
    Centroid(c: SphericalCap): Point3D
    {
        var h = c.CapHeight;
        var r = c.Sphere.Radius;
        var distance = 3.0 * (2.0 * r - h).Square / (4.0 * (3.0 * r - h));
        return c.Sphere.Center + c.Axis.Vector * distance;
    }

    // CONSERVATIVE, not tight: the whole sphere's bounds. A tight box would have to
    // decide, per world axis, whether the cap reaches that axis' extreme on the
    // sphere or is cut short by the base disk.
    // TODO(content): tighten to the cap's own extremes.
    Bounds(c: SphericalCap): Bounds3D
        => c.Sphere.Bounds;

    // True when the point lies in the ball AND within PolarAngle of the axis as
    // seen from the sphere's centre — the latter written as a plane test,
    // (p - C).axis >= R cos theta, which is exactly the cutting plane.
    Contains(c: SphericalCap, point: Point3D): Boolean
    {
        var v = c.Sphere.Center.Between(point);
        return v.MagnitudeSquared <= c.Sphere.Radius.Square
            && v.Dot(c.Axis.Vector) >= c.Sphere.Radius * c.PolarAngle.Cos;
    }

    //==
    // # Ellipsoid
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipsoid

    // (4/3) * pi * a * b * c. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipsoid#Volume
    Volume(e: Ellipsoid): Number
        => 4.0 / 3.0 * Number.Pi * e.SemiAxes.X * e.SemiAxes.Y * e.SemiAxes.Z;

    // APPROXIMATE. The surface area of a general ellipsoid is an incomplete
    // elliptic integral with no elementary closed form; this is KNUD THOMSEN'S
    // FORMULA,
    //     S ~= 4 pi ( ((ab)^p + (ac)^p + (bc)^p) / 3 ) ^ (1/p),   p = 1.6075,
    // whose relative error is at most 1.061% over ALL semi-axis ratios and is zero
    // for a sphere. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipsoid#Approximate_formula
    SurfaceArea(e: Ellipsoid): Number
    {
        var p = 1.6075;
        var ab = (e.SemiAxes.X * e.SemiAxes.Y).Pow(p);
        var ac = (e.SemiAxes.X * e.SemiAxes.Z).Pow(p);
        var bc = (e.SemiAxes.Y * e.SemiAxes.Z).Pow(p);
        return 4.0 * Number.Pi * ((ab + ac + bc) / 3.0).Pow(1.0 / p);
    }

    // The centre, by the ellipsoid's point symmetry.
    Centroid(e: Ellipsoid): Point3D
        => e.Center;
```
